why: Count the data: 5 coffees by 5 figure columns plus process, varietal and tasting notes, with totals that reconcile (72.0 kg in, 61.6 kg out, 14.4% loss), and notice that sold-out Guji stays in the table dimmed to ink-2 with its return date where the link was, that the close reuses that date as the next action, and that on phones the production columns drop out and each row becomes a small grid.

18 items and 7 item notes are set with no cards or icons: hierarchy comes only from a serif group head over a full ink rule, weight 500 names over 14% hairlines and a tabular price column, while a sticky side column holds the rules, so notice how notes such as 'Until 11am', 'From 11.30am' and 'Usually gone by 11' make it read as one kitchen's real day.

Hours are stored as data, in minutes from midnight, so one status() function covers every case in the shop's own time zone and today's row lifts by itself; notice the three columns each have one job (live sentence, seven-row table with a dated holiday closure under a full ink rule, address with two map buttons), and that Getting here and Access admit the step at the door and the downstairs toilet instead of saying 'easy to find'.

Three tiers split by hairlines carry 21 real values with no column of link lists: notice the wordmark over a computed next-roast stamp, hours re-edited for the footer (Wednesday to Friday merged, closed Monday last), and an allergen note where a generic footer puts empty legal links.

Compare with logo, links and a button: the strip names a dated deadline, the right slot shows live status from a minutes-from-midnight week, the bar picks its ground by testing which section sits under the 36px line, and on phones a clip-path sheet gives four 52px serif links with status, address and phone at the foot, so notice that one paint() fills every status slot, including the three live cells on the stone band.
